# Controls

19 controls: 12 `implemented`, 1 `procedural`, 6 `planned`, 0 `not-applicable`.

**A green check means the evidence resolves, not that it is sufficient.** `yarn lint:docs` proves that each anchor below exists at HEAD: the symbol is declared, the test title is present and not skipped in a tier a pull-request workflow runs, the workflow job exists and runs the named command, the heading is there. It does not prove that a test asserts what its control claims, that a threshold is right, or that a mapping to a clause is the best one. Those are judgements, and each sits beside its evidence so a reader can disagree with it.

**Coverage is not claimed.** The check asserts that every catalogued control has evidence, not that every clause of a framework has a control. Each framework section below says how many of its clauses no control here addresses.

† The ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A identifiers, titles and the count of 38 are taken from secondary sources — ISMS.online, "ISO 42001 Annex A Controls Explained" (https://www.isms.online/iso-42001/annex-a-controls/), and RiskProfs, "ISO 42001 Annex A Controls List: All 38 Controls Explained" (https://riskprofs.com/iso-42001-annex-a-controls-list/), which agree — and were not checked against the standard's text. A reader with the standard can correct them.

| Status           | Means                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `implemented`    | A test or a CI job fails if the control stops holding.                  |
| `procedural`     | A person enforces it by applying a written rule. No check does.         |
| `planned`        | Not delivered. The owner is the PRD that delivers it.                   |
| `not-applicable` | Excluded, with the justification a Statement of Applicability requires. |

## Frameworks

### NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

Registry id `nist-ai-rmf-1.0`, edition of 2023-01. Source: <https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1>.

**15 of 72 subcategories referenced; 57 not assessed.** Subcategory text copied from Tables 1–4 of the NIST PDF (GOVERN 19, MAP 18, MEASURE 22, MANAGE 13).

| Clause       | Text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Controls                              |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| GOVERN 1.4   | The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | CTL-DOC-01                            |
| GOVERN 3.2   | Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | CTL-HUM-01                            |
| GOVERN 4.3   | Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | CTL-LOG-01                            |
| MAP 3.5      | Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | CTL-HUM-01                            |
| MAP 4.1      | Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components – including the use of third-party data or software – are in place, followed, and documented, as are risks of infringement of a third party's intellectual property or other rights.                                                                                                                                                                        | CTL-DATA-01                           |
| MEASURE 1.1  | Approaches and metrics for measurement of AI risks enumerated during the MAP function are selected for implementation starting with the most significant AI risks. | MEASURE 2.5  | The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be valid and reliable. ### NIST AI 600-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework — Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile

Registry id `nist-ai-600-1`, edition of 2024-07. Source: <https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1>.

**4 of 213 suggested actions referenced; 209 not assessed.** Action text copied from the NIST PDF. The 213 is a count of unique GV-/MP-/MS-/MG-n.n-nnn ids in the PDF (GV 59, MP 39, MS 72, MG 43), including GV-4.3-001, which the PDF prints as "GV4.3--001".

| Clause     | Text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Controls    |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| MS-2.5-001 | Avoid extrapolating GAI system performance or capabilities from narrow, non-systematic, and anecdotal assessments.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | CTL-EVAL-01 |
| MS-2.7-001 | Apply established security measures to: Assess likelihood and magnitude of vulnerabilities and threats such as backdoors, compromised dependencies, data breaches, eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attacks, reverse engineering, autonomous agents, model theft or exposure of model weights, AI inference, bypass, extraction, and other baseline security concerns. | CTL-SUP-01  |
| MS-2.7-007 | Perform AI red-teaming to assess resilience against: Abuse to facilitate attacks on other systems (e.g., malicious code generation, enhanced phishing content), GAI attacks (e.g., prompt injection), ML attacks (e.g., adversarial examples/prompts, data poisoning, membership inference, model extraction, sponge examples).                                        | CTL-MEM-02  |
| MS-2.8-003 | Use digital content transparency solutions to enable the documentation of each instance where content is generated, modified, or shared to provide a tamper-proof history of the content, promote transparency, and enable traceability. Robust version control systems can also be applied to track changes across the AI lifecycle over time.                        | CTL-AUD-01  |

### OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025

Registry id `owasp-llm-2025`, edition of 2024-11. Source: <https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/>.

**7 of 10 risks referenced; 3 not assessed.** Titles and definitions copied from the risk pages under genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/. OWASP's 2026 edition renumbers this list (its LLM06 is Unbounded Consumption), so every ref keeps its :2025 suffix; mapping to the 2026 edition would be a new registry id.

| Clause     | Text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Controls                |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| LLM02:2025 | Sensitive Information Disclosure — "Sensitive information can affect both the LLM and its application context."                                                                                                                                        | CTL-SEC-01, CTL-DATA-01 |
| LLM03:2025 | Supply Chain — "LLM supply chains are susceptible to various vulnerabilities, which can affect the integrity of training data, models, and deployment platforms."                                                                                      | CTL-SUP-01              |
| LLM04:2025 | Data and Model Poisoning — "Data poisoning occurs when pre-training, fine-tuning, or embedding data is manipulated to introduce vulnerabilities, backdoors, or biases."                                                                                | CTL-MEM-01, CTL-MEM-02  |
| LLM05:2025 | Improper Output Handling — "insufficient validation, sanitization, and handling of the outputs generated by large language models before they are passed downstream to other components and systems."                                                  | CTL-OUT-01              |
| LLM06:2025 | Excessive Agency — "the vulnerability that enables damaging actions to be performed in response to unexpected, ambiguous or manipulated outputs from an LLM, regardless of what is causing the LLM to malfunction."                                    | CTL-AGY-01              |
| LLM08:2025 | Vector and Embedding Weaknesses — "Vectors and embeddings vulnerabilities present significant security risks in systems utilizing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with Large Language Models (LLMs)."                                             | CTL-MEM-02              |
| LLM10:2025 | Unbounded Consumption — "occurs when a Large Language Model (LLM) application allows users to conduct excessive and uncontrolled inferences, leading to risks such as denial of service (DoS), economic losses, model theft, and service degradation." | CTL-COST-01             |

### 45 CFR §164.312, Technical safeguards (HIPAA Security Rule)

Registry id `hipaa-164.312`, edition of 2026-09-24. Source: <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C/section-164.312>.

**6 of 12 standards and implementation specifications referenced; 6 not assessed.** Text copied from the eCFR as in force on 2026-09-24, the date given as its edition. The 12 are the five standards and seven implementation specifications of §164.312. The January 2025 NPRM (90 FR 898) is not final and is not mapped.

| Clause | Text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Controls   |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| (a)(1) | Standard, Access control — "Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4)." | CTL-ACC-01 |
| (b)    | Standard, Audit controls — "Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use electronic protected health information."                                                                                       | CTL-AUD-01 |
| (c)(1) | Standard, Integrity — "Implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction."                                                                                                                                              | CTL-AUD-01 |
| (c)(2) | Implementation specification, Mechanism to authenticate electronic protected health information (Addressable) — "Implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that electronic protected health information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner."                         | CTL-AUD-01 |
| (d)    | Standard, Person or entity authentication — "Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed."                                                                                                                 | CTL-ACC-01 |
| (e)(1) | Standard, Transmission security — "Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to electronic protected health information that is being transmitted over an electronic communications network."                                                                     | CTL-ACC-01 |
